walkthroughs.body_html:
Soil Systems & Terrestrial Food — a core area of Environmental Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Soil Systems & Terrestrial Food brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Soil Systems & Terrestrial Food.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Norman Borlaug, father of the Green Revolution, won the Nobel Peace Prize in:
Soil layer containing most organic matter:
options: O horizon
B horizon
C horizon
R horizon

mcqs.q: Why is atmospheric nitrogen unavailable to most plants directly?
options: Forest fires alone.
Because plants only use carbon.
N2 has a strong triple bond that most organisms cannot break.
Because plants cannot reach high enough to access it.

mcqs.q: What is the leading driver of global deforestation?
options: Agriculture (especially cattle ranching, soy, palm oil).
Predators have weaker immune systems.
Logging for timber and paper.
Forest fires alone.

mcqs.q: Why are top predators most affected by persistent pollutants like mercury?
options: Biomagnification concentrates pollutants at each trophic level up the food chain.
Predators are exposed to more pollution directly.
Predators have weaker immune systems.
Because plants only use carbon.
